question.problem: Find a vector that's tangent to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+2\sqrt{t}\,j+\sqrt{{t}^{2}+3}\,k$ at the point $P(1,2,2).$
question.worked_solution:
The point $P(1,2,2)$ is at the tip of $r(t)$ for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t.$ At this point, the vector ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})$ is tangent to the curve.

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to $P.$ We know that 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =i+2\,j+2\,k \\ t\,i+2\sqrt{t}\,j+\sqrt{{t}^{2}+3}\,k & =i+2\,j+2\,k,\end{aligned}
$$

and equating the coefficients of $i,j,$ and $k$ yields the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}t=1 \\ 2\sqrt{t}=2 \\ \sqrt{{t}^{2}+3}=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get $t=1.$ This value also satifies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(1,2,2)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+3})\,k \\  & =\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}\,j+\frac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+3}}\,k \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{(1)}}\,j+\frac{(1)}{\sqrt{(1)^{2}+3}}\,k \\  & =\,i+\,j+\frac{1}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, a tangent vector to the curve at the point $P(1,2,2)$ is $\,i+\,j+\frac{1}{2}\,k.$
